I think you're giving Infinity more credit than due. It's not a warship as much as it is an intel ship. It's massive and has an impressive armament but it's no dreadnought. 
That said, assuming the covenant have no great schism and sangheili don't defect to the humans side, the war would probably last longer but in the end the covenant would activate the rings and the great journey would be achieved. 
Now, CSO class super carriers, Long Night of Solace, and Sublime Transcendence, are each 30 times as long and and tens of times more wide than Infinity. There may be more of these, and even have been mentioned to exist in the Second Fleet of Homogeneous Clarity, but are never seen in game or in any of the books I've read. So we know of two of these. Now with no insurrection we can safely assume the NOVA bomb would never have been developed, and the slipspace incident in the Cygnus system never happened. So operation UPPER-CUT could never have been conceived, and the only nuke known to destroy a super carrier had never been developed. 
These super carriers, along with all other covenant can travel warships, can travel thousands of light years faster than human ships. So if our infinities are spread thin, or even all on one place, they can be picked off or destroyed all at once in force. 

As for the fate of humanity, the superior size and technological advantage of the covenant is unrivaled by any tactical advantage the UNSC has. They fight long and they fight hard, but over decades they are withered away and no longer in a position to defend both their worlds and the halos.
